newsitem.title: UK: Euro low sulphur jumps $5 on cargo deal to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Euro low sulphur jumps $5 on cargo deal to U.S..

text.p: European low sulphur fuel physical prices caught up with swaps on Friday with an eye-catching trader to trader cargo deal, dealers said.

A price of $95 a tonne fob was heard paid for 40,000 tonnes of British barrels by a trader believed to be trying to move material into the U.S. The deal, if confirmed, was a $5 hike on Thursday's levels.
June swaps finished at $95/$96 fob, with May just below. Dealers presumed the physical buyer had locked in a healthy paper spread.
The deal came amid scepticism the trans-atlantic arbitrage existed, even though New York harbour prices of more than $16 a barrel suggested it could be done.
Traders doubted demand in the U.S. for one percent cracked was strong enough to support much movement of material and no cargoes had been seen pointed there earlier in the day.
While the deal will help refinery margins it will displease a number of people pricing cargoes off quotes now.
High sulphur barge trade thinned out ahead of the European holiday weekend, losing $1 in value. Deals were seen at $83, $83.25 and $84 a tonne fob before offer levels lifted to $85.
"There was no real trend ahead of the weekend," said one trader. Bunker demand was poor, with most of the week's business done on Thursday. - London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
